text:
IncidentBot: P1 - model-serving error-rate spike detected in eu-west-1 (alerts: 5xx > 8% over 2m). Details: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-9821 :bangbang:
OncallBot: Paging @Alex and @Maria — primary oncall for eu-west-1. Pager sent.
Alex: Seeing the same. 5xx concentrated on /v1/generate - appears to be OOMs on a subset of pods. CPU fine, memory creeping. :thinking_face:
Maria: I’m still on call but heading to a meeting in ~8m. Want to do a quick handoff. Sam is incoming if we need takeover.
Alex: Okay — Maria, please confirm who will be driver & who will own comms after your handoff. I can stay on comms if you need me to.
Maria: Plan: Sam will be primary driver for the next 30m, Alex will be comms owner. I’ll stay as backup (secondary) for 10m post-handoff while I walk to the meeting. Does that work? @Sam @Alex
Sam: I can drive. Ready to take control. Need quick runbook pointer and any hot fixes you tried.
Maria: Steps so far: 1) rolled a config bump to increase pod memory requests (didn't stabilize) 2) scaled replicas from 8 -> 12 (partial improvement but error-rate still >5%) 3) rolled back latest model checkpoint last night (no change). No kernel panics in node logs.
Alex: Customer impact: traffic throttled for ~2% of requests in eu-west-1, higher latency for some tenants on generation routes. No full outages. Notifying SRE and support.
Jordan: tagging in from support side — prepping incident page and customer list. Will post an initial status to customers if we see sustained impact >10m.
Sam: Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.example/model-serving/oom-spike. Quick commands I’ll use:```
# check pod restarts
kubectl get pods -n model-svc -o wide --selector=app=model-serving
# tail one failing pod
kubectl logs -n model-svc <pod-name> -c model --since=10m
# trigger graceful drain on suspect node
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Maria: Also check the KV-cache eviction metrics and our prefix cache hit rates — those dropped right before the spike. Link to graphs: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/cache-metrics
Alex: Confirming comms: I’ll post initial status in #incidents and ping support with the known customer list. Jordan, coordinate any outbound comms; we’ll keep updates every 10m or on milestone.
Sam: Taking driver. I’ll start triage with failing pod logs + node memory metrics, and attempt a restart cycle on the worst offenders. If restarts don't drop errors in 5m I’ll scale up to 18 replicas (with throttling policy).
Maria: FYI — APAC coverage gap from 02:00-03:00 UTC today, no primary there. If this spreads to APAC I might not be able to rejoin for full takeover. Sam, if you need additional hands escalate to oncall paging.
OncallBot: Noted coverage gap window for APAC in schedule. If escalation occurs, oncall paging will follow standard escalation (primary -> secondary -> oncall rotation).
Jordan: Got it. Drafting customer note now. Will wait for Alex to sign off before send.
Alex: Go ahead and prep, Jordan. Send only after the 10m check if error rate hasn't dropped below 2%. Post draft here and I’ll review.
Sam: First triage pass: identified 3 pods with OOMKill in logs 3m ago; nodes show kernel OOM events correlated with large batch requests. Temporarily applying pod anti-affinity to spread load and restarting the 3 pods now.
Maria: Thanks Sam — handing off formally. I’m good to hand primary to Sam now. Alex stays comms. I’ll monitor for another 6 minutes then drop out. :white_check_mark:
Alex: Acknowledged handoff. Sam driving, Alex comms, Maria backup for 6m, Jordan on customer comms. Recording assignments in incident doc.
IncidentBot: Incident status updated: driver=Sam, comms=Alex, backup=Maria, support=Jordan. Next status update due in 8 minutes. :clipboard:
